correctness.rationale: For every odd prime and all positions of the specified form, the affine-unit reduction is invertible; exact three off-diagonal Fourier equations split into two independent positive zero-sum polygons and equal parity mass. Positivity excludes 1–2 vertices per parity; strict three-vertex relations are exactly triangles containing the origin, with unique normalized sine barycentric coordinates. Inclusion-exclusion counts every admissible cyclic gap triple without overcounting. The standard-library checker separately solves barycentric linear equations and directly verifies 29,223 complex Gram entries for p=3,5,7,11, corroborating the unrestricted proof; the computation alone is not the proof.

value.rationale: The sharp minimization of distinct harmonic sampling frequencies with positive adjustable gains is natural for exact Parseval reconstruction on a sparse three-site set. The theorem gives a uniform six-frequency optimum for arbitrarily large odd primes, versus all 2p characters if the gains are fixed equal, and completely classifies and counts optimal masks with unique weights. Thus the result is not merely a generic convexity exercise or arbitrary finite census.
